newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Food poisoning takes toll in southern China.
newsitem.headline: Food poisoning takes toll in southern China.

text.p: An outbreak of food poisoning in south China, feared linked to rat poison, has killed one child and put nearly 100 children in hospital, Hong Kong newspapers reported on Monday.

A four-year-old girl died on Saturday after eating part of a chicken that had died from rat poison, the China-backed Ta Kung Pao reported, quoting hospital sources and neighbours of the girl in Guangdong province.
A boy aged one-and-a-half was fighting for his life on a respirator and doctors feared he would be reduced to "a vegetable", the newspaper said.
Another newspaper, Ming Pao, reported that 96 children had been admitted to hospitals in the past few days after they complained of stomach pains and fever.
Their condition was stable, the newspaper said, adding that investigations were continuing to see if the cases were linked to rat poison.
